# NAGI 凪
## Japan Market-Entry Campaign — Sleep-Quality & Temporary-Stress Supplement
### Ethical Design Document, Creative Platform & Activation Plan
**Prepared for Brand Council | Version 2.0 (supersedes v1.0 "Just a Little Calmer Tonight")**

---

> ⚠️ **Compliance and status caveat.** Japanese food-labelling and advertising law is in active reform following the 2024 red-yeast-rice (紅麹) incident. Every legal reference in this document is a **planning input, not a legal opinion**. No claim string, label, pack, script or landing page may be published until (a) Japanese regulatory counsel has signed the specific asset in writing and (b) the wording matches the accepted notification record. Figures marked *[ILL]* are illustrative planning numbers to be replaced with primary research and counsel confirmation in Gate 0. Assumptions and confidence levels are registered in §14.
>
> **Planning FX rate: ¥155 = US$1.00**, fixed for this document; re-fixed at each gate.

---

## 1. The Idea, in One Page

### 1.1 The consumer truth we are building on

Japanese adults do not experience poor sleep as an *illness*. They experience it as a slow erosion — a run of mornings that start badly, a 15:00 fog, a shortening fuse with a spouse or a subordinate. They do not want to be rescued. They want the run to break.

Crucially, the culturally available frame for this already exists and is centuries old: **未病 (mibyō)** — "not yet ill, not quite well" — and **養生 (yōjō)** — the daily cultivation of health. These are not exotic decorations. They are the ordinary, respectable, non-medical vocabulary in which a 48-year-old section manager can admit he sleeps badly without admitting he is unwell, and can do something about it without going to a clinic.

### 1.2 The brand idea

> **凪 (nagi)** is the still interval when the land breeze and the sea breeze change places — the pause between two winds. It is not a permanent calm. It is the gap that lets the next thing begin.

That is an honest metaphor for what this product does: a small, repeated, cumulative intervention. It is also, precisely, what the science supports and what the law permits us to say.

### 1.3 Campaign platform

**「いい朝が、すこしずつ増える。」**
*"Little by little, more good mornings."*

**Why this line and not v1.0's "Just a Little Calmer Tonight."** The previous line was rejected in redraft for a specific reason: *tonight* promises an acute, same-night effect. Our positioning is maintenance, not rescue; our notified claim is a continuity claim requiring daily intake; and an acute-relief promise edges toward drug-efficacy territory under 薬機法. The line contradicted the strategy and the dossier. The replacement line is **cumulative** ("little by little"), **counted in mornings not nights** (an outcome the user can actually verify), and **quantitatively modest** ("more," not "good mornings, guaranteed").

**Endline / signature:** 「夜は、すこし静かに。」 — used only as an atmospheric sign-off, never as a claim.

### 1.4 The proof architecture (why anyone should believe us)

| Layer | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Notified function** | The exact CAA-notified claim string, verbatim | Pack front, all claim-bearing assets |
| **The honest number** | Plain-Japanese statement of the *size* of the effect and the proportion of people who saw it | Pack QR → "この製品でわかっていること" page |
| **The dossier** | Full systematic review / trial record, Japanese, downloadable, plus the studies that did *not* support us | Same page, no email gate |
| **The refund** | 「合わない方へ」 — 60-day full refund, no return, no reason required (D2C) | Pack, site, all D2C creative |
| **The referral out** | Sleep self-check that routes likely clinical cases to medical care, *before* the buy button | Site, LINE, pharmacy leaflet |

No competitor in this category currently publishes its negative studies or routes traffic away from purchase. That, not adjective inflation, is our distinctiveness.

---

## 2. Market, Consumer and Competitive Reality

### 2.1 Why Japan is a distinctive advertising market

| Dimension | Japan-specific reality | Campaign implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Category maturity** | Large, habituated supplement market; supplements read as *maintenance* (養生), not *rescue* | Sell routine and continuity |
| **Health philosophy** | 未病 / 養生 inherited from Kampō; wellness is a daily practice, not an intervention | Position in the mibyō space — legitimate and non-medical |
| **Trust position** | Post-紅麹 scrutiny of the self-notified FFC regime; tightened adverse-event reporting and GMP requirements | Radical transparency is the differentiator, not a cost |
| **Advertising register** | Superlatives and hard-sell read as vulgar and untrustworthy; *情緒 (jōcho)* — atmospheric, indirect, feeling-led advertising — is the prestige register | Craft-led, quiet, low-volume creative |
| **Retail structure** | Drugstore chains (マツキヨココカラ, ウエルシア, ツルハ, サンドラッグ, コスモス) are the gatekeepers; shelf and 什器 presence drive trial more than awareness | Trade investment is not "below the line," it *is* the line |
| **Word-of-mouth power** | Category breakouts are 口コミ-driven, amplified by X and 店頭 | Highest legal/ethical exposure sits here (§8.4) |

### 2.2 Audience: four named segments, not "adults 28–55"

| # | Segment | Size *[ILL]* | Sleep problem | Receptivity | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **「中間管理職の睡眠負債」** — 42–55, male-skewed (~65/35), mid-management, commuter, ¥7–12M HH income | 6.2M | Early waking, 3am rumination, no wind-down; will not consult a doctor about sleep | High to non-medical, dignity-preserving framing; hostile to anything that looks like weakness | **P1** |
| **B** | **「途切れる眠りの母」** — 33–44, female, dual-income, child under 8 | 4.1M | Fragmented sleep, low agency over schedule; guilt about self-spend | High to *permission* framing ("this is maintenance, not indulgence"); very high 口コミ propensity | **P1** |
| **C** | **「夜更かしの自律」** — 26–34, female-skewed, single/DINK, high screen-time | 5.5M | Self-imposed late nights, "revenge bedtime"; sleep as self-optimisation | High to design/ritual framing; lowest willingness to pay; entry cohort | P2 |
| **D** | **交代勤務者** — nurses, care workers, logistics, retail | 3.8M | Circadian disruption, genuinely severe | Commercially attractive, **ethically constrained** | **P3 — deliberately not targeted** |

**Why we will not target Segment D.** Their sleep disruption is structural and often clinically significant; a continuity claim built on nocturnal sleep quality is a poor fit for rotating shifts; and marketing a mild supplement into a population with elevated genuine sleep-disorder prevalence risks displacing care. They may buy the product — we will not exclude them from shelves — but we will run **no targeted media, no shift-worker creative, and no occupational-health B2B push into shift-heavy employers in Years 1–2.** This costs us revenue. It is recorded in §10 and audited in §11.

**Primary target for Year 1: Segments A and B.** Creative lead: A. Advocacy engine: B.

### 2.3 Competitive set — the real problem we face

| Competitor | Proposition | Why it matters to us |
|---|---|---|
| **Yakult 1000 / Y1000** | Lactic-acid-bacterium drink; notified stress-relief and sleep-quality claims; category-defining 口コミ breakout | Redefined "sleep quality" as a mainstream, non-medical, *drinkable ritual*. It owns the ritual, has a delivery-lady route to home, and dominates conversational share. We are a capsule competing with a habit. |
| **味の素 グリナ** | Glycine, sleep quality; long-running, D2C-strong, medically credible tone | Owns the "serious sleep supplement" credibility position among 50+. |
| **アサヒ ネナイト** | L-theanine tablet, mass drugstore distribution, low price | Direct format and ingredient overlap; our price premium must be earned, not asserted. |
| **ハウス ネルノダ** | GABA drink, konbini-led, impulse | Owns immediacy and convenience — precisely the acute position we are declining. |
| **FANCL / DHC / 小林製薬 ナイトミン** | Trusted domestic houses, decades of equity, deep drugstore relationships | Trust equity we cannot buy. We can only buy *verifiability*. |
| **Suntory Wellness** | Premium D2C machine, CRM excellence | Sets the benchmark on subscription economics and 顧客対応. |

**The competitive conclusion.** We cannot out-spend, out-trust or out-distribute the domestic incumbents in Year 1. There is exactly one position they have structurally declined to occupy: **published, checkable, effect-size-honest ev

# Warehouse Automation & Workforce Transition Roadmap
### Five-Site Network — Board Decision Document

---

## 0. Executive Summary and Decision Ask

**What we are recommending.** A five-year, gated, differentiated automation program. Two sites get flexible robotics (Rung 3). One gets mechanization only. One gets process/digital fixes and a network-role decision. The anchor-town site — which is also our highest-volume site — gets the deepest automation but is deliberately sequenced last and designed to *grow into* its automation rather than shrink into it. All five sites get the low-capital error-and-ergonomics package first.

**What we are explicitly rejecting.** (a) The vendors' 3-year payback, which excludes ramp, dual-running, transition cost, and technical staffing; (b) uniform automation across five structurally different sites; (c) any big-bang cutover; (d) a headcount plan that relies on layoffs at the anchor town.

**The decision ask today:**

| Item | Amount | Trigger for next tranche |
|---|---|---|
| **Authorize now: Wave 0** (network-wide error-proofing, data remediation, PMO, forensic study, architecture & vendor selection, front-end engineering for Site A) | **$11.5M** ($7.5M capex / $4.0M opex) | — |
| Indicative envelope, full program through Year 6 (for planning, **not** authorized today) | $92M ($74M capex / $18M transition opex) | Each wave released only on written gate closure |
| Peak net cash trough (worst point of cumulative outflow, base case, ~month 30) | **$34M** | This, not total capex, is the capital constraint that binds |
| Probability-weighted NPV @ 12% hurdle, 15-year horizon | **+$19.5M** | Re-forecast at each gate with actual data |

**The four questions the brief asked, answered in one line each:**

1. **Degree and sequence per site** — §3 table: Site A (Rung 3, Wave 1) → Site B (Rung 3, Wave 2) and Site C (Rung 2, parallel) → Site E (Rung 3 + conditional Rung 4, Wave 3) → Site D (Rung 1 + network-role decision, Wave 4). One robotics conversion migration in flight at a time, ever.
2. **Workforce** — a published, signed Workforce Compact with a 5-year tenure guarantee; four named destinations for every affected employee; net –345 FTE over five years achieved with **≤10 involuntary separations in the planned scenario**, funded by an $18M transition budget that is cheaper than one botched cutover.
3. **Service protection** — parallel run, SKU-tranche then customer-tranche migration, permanent reduced manual fallback, 110–120% network capacity during conversion, hard peak blackout, 25% vendor payment held back against 90 days at design rate, and any gate-committee member can hold a golive.
4. **Measurement** — three metric layers (financial, operational/customer, workforce), Finance-owned benefit realization against a frozen baseline, a board one-page scorecard, and independent post-implementation audits at 12 and 24 months per site with a capital-reallocation rule when a wave misses.

# "Just a Little Calmer Tonight"
### Market-Entry Marketing Campaign — Sleep & Stress Supplement, Japan
**Ethical Design Document + Activation Plan | Prepared for Brand Council Approval**

---

## 0. Executive Summary

**Market selected:** Japan (national, Tokyo/Osaka/Nagoya weighted).
**Product:** *NAGI Night* — a magnesium + L‑theanine + GABA capsule positioned on **sleep quality and temporary stress relief** for working adults aged 28–55.
**Regulatory pathway:** Notified **Food with Function Claims (機能性表示食品 / FFC)** — not a drug, not a FOSHU.

**The strategic insight that drives everything below:** In Japan, the culturally preferred advertising register (understatement, modesty, indirectness, evidence-by-process), the legally permitted claim language (*"it has been reported that…"*), and the scientifically honest description of what a supplement actually does (a small, incremental improvement in sleep quality for some people) **all point in the same direction.** Most markets force a trade-off between persuasive power, legal safety, and truthfulness. Japan does not. Our campaign is built on exploiting that rare alignment rather than fighting it.

**Consequence:** we compete on *trust*, not on *promise size*. This is also a commercial necessity. Following the 2024 red‑yeast‑rice (紅麹) adverse‑event crisis at a major Japanese pharmaceutical company, consumer confidence in the entire supplement category — and specifically in the notification-based FFC regime — was materially damaged, and the regulatory regime was tightened (mandatory adverse-event reporting; GMP requirements phasing in for supplement-form FFC products). A hype-led launch in this environment is not merely unethical; it is commercially self-defeating.

**Approval ask (illustrative, ¥):**

| Gate | Scope | Spend | Release condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gate 0 — authorize now** | Substantiation dossier, FFC notification, trademark/naming clearance, GMP audit, JARO/legal pre-clearance, qualitative consumer research, trade education build, crisis playbook | **¥120M** | — |
| Gate 1 | Seed launch (Apr–May), pharmacy channel, PR, owned/LINE | ¥180M | Notification accepted; 100% claim-matrix legal sign-off; adverse-event system live |
| Gate 2 | National paid media build (Jun–Sep) | ¥380M | Repeat-purchase ≥28% at month 3; zero substantiated claim complaints; disclosure audit 100% |
| Gate 3 | Scale + corporate wellness B2B2E + EC subscription (Oct–Mar) | ¥270M | Ethical KPI dashboard all-green (§11); subscription cancellation UX audited |
| **Year-1 total (indicative)** | | **¥950M (≈US$6.3M)** | Gated, not pre-committed |

**What we explicitly reject:** (a) translated global creative; (b) celebrity/idol endorsement in Year 1; (c) "¥500 trial" subscription funnels; (d) physician or clinic endorsement framing; (e) before/after and fear-of-*karōshi* imagery; (f) any claim implying treatment of insomnia or replacement of sleep or medical care; (g) "No.1" claims of any kind in Year 1.

> ⚠️ **Compliance caveat:** Japanese advertising and food-labelling rules change frequently, and the FFC regime is in active reform. Every legal statement in this document is a planning input, not an opinion. All claim wording, labelling, and disclosure mechanics must be confirmed in writing by Japanese regulatory counsel and the product's notification record before any asset is published.

---

## 1. Why Japan, and What Makes It Distinctive

| Dimension | Japan-specific reality | Campaign implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Category size & habit** | Large, mature supplement market with high daily-habit adherence; supplements are treated as *maintenance*, not *rescue* | Sell routine and continuity, not transformation |
| **Health philosophy** | Deep-rooted concepts of **養生 (yōjō** — cultivating health daily) and **未病 (mibyō** — "not yet ill, not quite well"), inherited from Kampō | Position in the *mibyō* space: legitimate, non-medical, culturally native |
| **Trust deficit** | Post-2024 category trust shock; heightened scrutiny of FFC self-notification | Radical transparency is the differentiator |
| **Advertising norms** | Hard-sell and superlatives read as vulgar/untrustworthy; *jōcho* (emotional, atmospheric) advertising is preferred; strong dislike of pressure | Soft, quiet, craft-led creative; low-volume CT

# Critique — "Just a Little Calmer Tonight" (NAGI Night, Japan)

## 1. Headline judgment

What exists is unusually well-grounded for a market-entry brief: the regulatory pathway is correctly named, the cultural framing (*yōjō*, *mibyō*, *jōcho*) is real rather than decorative, and the post-紅麹 trust context is the right strategic pivot. That is the good news, and it is genuinely good.

The bad news is that **this is not yet a campaign.** The document terminates mid-word in §1 ("low-volume CT…"), and §11 is cited in a gate condition but does not exist. Everything the request actually asked for — creative platform, channel/media plan, message architecture, measurement, ethical safeguards in operation — is either referenced or absent. What has been delivered is an executive summary plus the opening of a market-context table: roughly 15% of a document that promises eleven sections.

---

## 2. Blocking issues

**2.1 Incompleteness.** Sections 2–11 must be written before this can be assessed as a response to the brief. In particular: the creative concept, the claim matrix, the channel plan, the crisis playbook (invoked in Gate 0), and the ethical KPI dashboard (invoked in Gate 2 and 3 release conditions) are all load-bearing and all missing.

**2.2 Factual error — JARO does not pre-clear advertising.** "JARO/legal pre-clearance" in Gate 0 misdescribes the institution. JARO (日本広告審査機構) is a complaint-handling self-regulatory body; it does not issue prior approvals. Actual pre-clearance in Japan runs through (a) broadcaster 考査 (kōsa) against JBA/NAB-Japan codes, (b) industry bodies such as JHNFA (日本健康・栄養食品協会) and JADMA for mail-order, and (c) outside regulatory counsel. Fix the mechanism, not just the acronym — the whole Gate 0 clearance workflow depends on it.

**2.3 Formulation may not be notifiable as described.** The FFC scheme has historically excluded, as the *functional component*, nutrients for which Dietary Reference Intakes / nutrient function claims already exist — which puts **magnesium** in a difficult position as a headline functional ingredient. GABA and L-theanine are heavily notified and defensible; magnesium likely is not, and may only ride along as a non-functional nutrient. This is not a wording nit: the product's lead descriptor and possibly the dossier strategy are built on it. Confirm with counsel before anything else, and state a fallback formulation/claim architecture.

**2.4 Stealth-marketing regulation is not named.** Japan's ステマ規制 took effect 1 October 2023 under the Premiums and Representations Act, designating undisclosed advertiser-influenced content as a misleading representation, with 「広告」/「PR」 disclosure obligations. A campaign leaning on LINE, owned social and (inevitably) UGC/word-of-mouth cannot treat this as "disclosure audit 100%" without naming the rule, the disclosure standard, the contract clauses that bind creators, and who audits. Given that Yakult 1000's sleep/stress success in Japan was substantially word-of-mouth-driven, this is where the campaign's biggest ethical and legal exposure will sit.

**2.5 No entity/importer structure.** A non-resident company generally cannot be the FFC notifier. There is no mention of the Japanese notifying entity, the 表示責任者, food import notification (食品等輸入届), Japanese-language labelling, or distributor structure. For a *market-entry* plan this is a substantive operational hole, not an appendix item.

---

## 3. Regulatory precision gaps

- **Legal basis is never cited.** Health Promotion Act Art. 65 (exaggerated health claims), 薬機法 Art. 68 (unapproved drug-efficacy claims), 景表法 (misleading representations, plus the 課徴金 surcharge and 確約手続 regimes) should anchor the "what we reject" list. Right now the rejections read as taste, when several are legal requirements.
- **不実証広告規制 (景表法 Art. 7(2))**: the CAA can demand substantiation within ~15 days. This creates a hard operational spec — the dossier must be *retrievable and defensible in 15 days*, in Japanese, at all times. Nowhere stated.

# NAGI 凪
## Japan Market-Entry Campaign — Sleep-Quality & Temporary-Stress Supplement
### Ethical Design Document, Creative Platform & Activation Plan
**Prepared for Brand Council | Version 2.0 (supersedes v1.0 "Just a Little Calmer Tonight")**

---

> ⚠️ **Compliance and status caveat.** Japanese food-labelling and advertising law is in active reform following the 2024 red-yeast-rice (紅麹) incident. Every legal reference in this document is a **planning input, not a legal opinion**. No claim string, label, pack, script or landing page may be published until (a) Japanese regulatory counsel has signed the specific asset in writing and (b) the wording matches the accepted notification record. Figures marked *[ILL]* are illustrative planning numbers to be replaced with primary research and counsel confirmation in Gate 0. Assumptions and confidence levels are registered in §14.
>
> **Planning FX rate: ¥155 = US$1.00**, fixed for this document; re-fixed at each gate.

---

## 1. The Idea, in One Page

### 1.1 The consumer truth we are building on

Japanese adults do not experience poor sleep as an *illness*. They experience it as a slow erosion — a run of mornings that start badly, a 15:00 fog, a shortening fuse with a spouse or a subordinate. They do not want to be rescued. They want the run to break.

Crucially, the culturally available frame for this already exists and is centuries old: **未病 (mibyō)** — "not yet ill, not quite well" — and **養生 (yōjō)** — the daily cultivation of health. These are not exotic decorations. They are the ordinary, respectable, non-medical vocabulary in which a 48-year-old section manager can admit he sleeps badly without admitting he is unwell, and can do something about it without going to a clinic.

### 1.2 The brand idea

> **凪 (nagi)** is the still interval when the land breeze and the sea breeze change places — the pause between two winds. It is not a permanent calm. It is the gap that lets the next thing begin.

That is an honest metaphor for what this product does: a small, repeated, cumulative intervention. It is also, precisely, what the science supports and what the law permits us to say.

### 1.3 Campaign platform

**「いい朝が、すこしずつ増える。」**
*"Little by little, more good mornings."*

**Why this line and not v1.0's "Just a Little Calmer Tonight."** The previous line was rejected in redraft for a specific reason: *tonight* promises an acute, same-night effect. Our positioning is maintenance, not rescue; our notified claim is a continuity claim requiring daily intake; and an acute-relief promise edges toward drug-efficacy territory under 薬機法. The line contradicted the strategy and the dossier. The replacement line is **cumulative** ("little by little"), **counted in mornings not nights** (an outcome the user can actually verify), and **quantitatively modest** ("more," not "good mornings, guaranteed").

**Endline / signature:** 「夜は、すこし静かに。」 — used only as an atmospheric sign-off, never as a claim.

### 1.4 The proof architecture (why anyone should believe us)

| Layer | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Notified function** | The exact CAA-notified claim string, verbatim | Pack front, all claim-bearing assets |
| **The honest number** | Plain-Japanese statement of the *size* of the effect and the proportion of people who saw it | Pack QR → "この製品でわかっていること" page |
| **The dossier** | Full systematic review / trial record, Japanese, downloadable, plus the studies that did *not* support us | Same page, no email gate |
| **The refund** | 「合わない方へ」 — 60-day full refund, no return, no reason required (D2C) | Pack, site, all D2C creative |
| **The referral out** | Sleep self-check that routes likely clinical cases to medical care, *before* the buy button | Site, LINE, pharmacy leaflet |

No competitor in this category currently publishes its negative studies or routes traffic away from purchase. That, not adjective inflation, is our distinctiveness.

---

## 2. Market, Consumer and Competitive Reality

### 2.1 Why Japan is a distinctive advertising market

| Dimension | Japan-specific reality | Campaign implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Category maturity** | Large, habituated supplement market; supplements read as *maintenance* (養生), not *rescue* | Sell routine and continuity |
| **Health philosophy** | 未病 / 養生 inherited from Kampō; wellness is a daily practice, not an intervention | Position in the mibyō space — legitimate and non-medical |
| **Trust position** | Post-紅麹 scrutiny of the self-notified FFC regime; tightened adverse-event reporting and GMP requirements | Radical transparency is the differentiator, not a cost |
| **Advertising register** | Superlatives and hard-sell read as vulgar and untrustworthy; *情緒 (jōcho)* — atmospheric, indirect, feeling-led advertising — is the prestige register | Craft-led, quiet, low-volume creative |
| **Retail structure** | Drugstore chains (マツキヨココカラ, ウエルシア, ツルハ, サンドラッグ, コスモス) are the gatekeepers; shelf and 什器 presence drive trial more than awareness | Trade investment is not "below the line," it *is* the line |
| **Word-of-mouth power** | Category breakouts are 口コミ-driven, amplified by X and 店頭 | Highest legal/ethical exposure sits here (§8.4) |

### 2.2 Audience: four named segments, not "adults 28–55"

| # | Segment | Size *[ILL]* | Sleep problem | Receptivity | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **「中間管理職の睡眠負債」** — 42–55, male-skewed (~65/35), mid-management, commuter, ¥7–12M HH income | 6.2M | Early waking, 3am rumination, no wind-down; will not consult a doctor about sleep | High to non-medical, dignity-preserving framing; hostile to anything that looks like weakness | **P1** |

| **C** | **「夜更かしの自律」** — 26–34, female-skewed, single/DINK, high screen-time | 5.5M | Self-imposed late nights, "revenge bedtime"; sleep as self-optimisation | High to design/ritual framing; lowest willingness to pay; entry cohort | P2 |
| **D** | **交代勤務者** — nurses, care workers, logistics, retail | 3.8M | Circadian disruption, genuinely severe | Commercially attractive, **ethically constrained** | **P3 — deliberately not targeted** |

**Why we will not target Segment D.** Their sleep disruption is structural and often clinically significant; a continuity claim built on nocturnal sleep quality is a poor fit for rotating shifts; and marketing a mild supplement into a population with elevated genuine sleep-disorder prevalence risks displacing care. They may buy the product — we will not exclude them from shelves — but we will run **no targeted media, no shift-worker creative, and no occupational-health B2B push into shift-heavy employers in Years 1–2.** This costs us revenue. It is recorded in §10 and audited in §11.

**Primary target for Year 1: Segments A and B.** Creative lead: A. Advocacy engine: B.

### 2.3 Competitive set — the real problem we face

| Competitor | Proposition | Why it matters to us |
|---|---|---|
| **Yakult 1000 / Y1000** | Lactic-acid-bacterium drink; notified stress-relief and sleep-quality claims; category-defining 口コミ breakout | Redefined "sleep quality" as a mainstream, non-medical, *drinkable ritual*. It owns the ritual, has a delivery-lady route to home, and dominates conversational share. We are a capsule competing with a habit. |
| **味の素 グリナ** | Glycine, sleep quality; long-running, D2C-strong, medically credible tone | Owns the "serious sleep supplement" credibility position among 50+. |
| **アサヒ ネナイト** | L-theanine tablet, mass drugstore distribution, low price | Direct format and ingredient overlap; our price premium must be earned, not asserted. |
| **ハウス ネルノダ** | GABA drink, konbini-led, impulse | Owns immediacy and convenience — precisely the acute position we are declining. |
| **FANCL / DHC / 小林製薬 ナイトミン** | Trusted domestic houses, decades of equity, deep drugstore relationships | Trust equity we cannot buy. We can only buy *verifiability*. |
| **Suntory Wellness** | Premium D2C machine, CRM excellence | Sets the benchmark on subscription economics and 顧客対応. |

**The competitive conclusion.** We cannot out-spend, out-trust or out-distribute the domestic incumbents in Year 1. There is exactly one position they have structurally declined to occupy: **published, checkable, effect-size-honest ev
